correctnessFindings.assessment: A service-wide pending allowance charges backing ArrayBuffer bytes and frame count across the current and predecessor workers: 8 MiB or 1024 frames. Empty input does not transfer. Cumulative consumed-byte/frame acknowledgments avoid retaining a callback per feed.

Acknowledgments are validated as safe monotonic values within the owned worker posted range. Failed post before transfer rolls back; uncertain transfer and unresolved termination retain debt. Exit or successful termination releases ownership, including after lifecycle code removed listeners.

Desktop microphone capture uses 4096 mono Float32 samples per frame, or 16384 bytes. The 8 MiB limit therefore allows 512 fully unconsumed desktop frames: about 43.7 seconds at 48 kHz, 47.6 seconds at 44.1 kHz, or 131.1 seconds at 16 kHz. The 1024-frame cap becomes decisive for smaller frames.

Overflow initiates stop before emitting the error, preventing reentrant feed acceptance. Desktop onError immediately clears activeSessionId, stops capture, and discards buffered capture audio; later final events from already-admitted worker audio fail the active-session check. Already inserted text remains.

The mobile/remote controller records the error, refuses later feed, and rejects finish rather than returning a successful transcript. Worker stop is FIFO after admitted audio, but the existing 60-second stop deadline can terminate a stuck worker; even a worker that drains is not an end-to-end preservation guarantee after the desktop error.

originalReview.userVisibleBeforeAfter: A local recognizer that falls sufficiently behind now stops dictation and reports that it cannot keep up. Newly captured audio is discarded and accepted-but-not-yet-delivered transcript can be lost after the frontend clears the active session. Previously inserted text stays in place.
originalReview.capacityAndDataLoss: New 8 MiB/1024-frame in-flight audio allowance. It accounts for full backing allocations, including subarray backing storage. It does not bound native recognizer/model memory, renderer IPC queues, or all process RSS. Cloud dictation is unchanged.

platformEvidence.assessment: The worker accounting uses common Node worker_threads APIs. Historical stalled-worker controls use real Node/Electron workers with controlled recognizers; no native speech model or real microphone overload was run on macOS, Linux, and Windows. Actual desktop capture cadence is established from the exact-head 4096-sample caller, not inferred from a synthetic test feed.
platformEvidence.executedHost: Fresh shared batch: macOS darwin arm64; Node 26.6.0. PRs outside that batch have no new execution in this follow-up.

originalReview.sshAndFolderCases: The execution host retains worker ownership and the mobile/remote dictation controller receives the existing error channel. Added consumption fields are internal worker messages, not a new remote stream opcode. Folder workspaces require no Git-specific behavior.

regressionCoverage.limitations: No user-flow test proves transcript recovery after overload, and current code does not preserve all admitted transcript on that path. A native call that will not terminate can retain predecessor debt; restarting does not manufacture a fresh budget. Native speech latency and all-platform execution remain gaps.
